statements.t: We expect our sales to increase in the next 12 months as our customers expand the number of models in which they include our battery systems for the new model year and as we continue to grow into new markets, including trucking and industrials, with new product offerings.

Moreover, we expect the focus of the Dakota Lithium brand on retail sales to restore that channel for the Company moving forward, with such assets expected to contribute material revenue beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.
We expect incremental operating costs in order to restore Dakota Lithium’s commercial operations ahead of its expected revenue contribution.
We believe that our solid-state technology design allows for a much safer, more efficient battery cell that we believe will be a key differentiator in the energy storage market.

As discussed under “ Liquidity and Capital Resources ” below we expect that we will need to raise additional funds, including through the use of the ATM (as defined below) and the issuance of equity, equity-related or debt securities or by obtaining additional credit from financial institutions to fund, together with our principal sources of liquidity, ongoing costs.

If such financings are not available, or if the terms of such financings are less desirable than we expect, we may be forced to take actions to reduce our capital or operating expenditures, including not seeking potential acquisition opportunities, eliminating redundancies, or reducing or delaying our production facility expansions, reduce operations, sell off our assets, seek the protection of bankruptcy courts…

In connection with any future equity offerings, we will be required to use 50% of the net proceeds from such offering to redeem outstanding shares of the Series B Preferred Stock at the Optional Redemption Price.
We will pay Canaccord a commission of 3.0% of the aggregate gross proceeds from each sale of shares of common stock and will reimburse Canaccord for certain specified expenses.

Under the Series B Waiver, the Company is required to pay cash dividends equal to 2% per annum on or prior to October 1, 2026 and cash dividends equal to 6% per annum on or prior to October 30, 2026, and payment-in-kind dividends will continue to accrue at a rate of 2% per annum.

An increasing proportion of our sales has been and is expected to continue to be derived from sales to RV OEMs, driven by continued efforts to develop and expand sales to RV OEMs with whom we have longstanding relationships.
Our RV OEM sales have been on a purchase order basis, without firm revenue commitments, and we expect that this will likely continue to be the case.
We expect that direct to consumer sales will remain relatively flat through 2026.

However, we expect growth among our existing RV OEM customers to be driven by expanded adoption of our products across additional models and configurations, as well as increased system content per unit, rather than solely by changes in overall RV shipment volumes.

In addition, we anticipate increased revenue from continued expansion within existing customer relationships across other end markets, including industrial and commercial energy storage applications and the heavy-duty trucking market, where fleet customers have begun to adopt our systems and expand deployments following initial pilot programs.

As we look toward the production of our solid-state cells, we have signed a Commercial Offtake Agreement with a lithium mining company located in Nevada for the supply of lithium, which we expect will enable us to further manage our cost of goods over time.

In any particular period, changes in the mix and volume of particular products sold and the prices of those products relative to other products will impact our average selling price and our cost of goods sold.

We expect accessory sales to increase as we further develop full-system design expertise and product offerings and consumers increasingly demand more sophisticated systems, rather than simple drop-in replacements.
Consistent with our operating history, we plan to continue to automate additional aspects of our battery production lines.

Although our automation efforts are expected to reduce our costs of goods, we may not fully recognize the anticipated savings when planned and could experience additional costs or disruptions to our production activities.

As we continue to expand into new markets, develop new products and move towards production of our own conventional LFP cells and, in the longer term, solid state cells, we will experience competition with a wider range of companies.

Our competitors may be able to source materials and components at lower costs, which may require us to evaluate measures to reduce our own costs, lower the price of our products or increase sales volumes in order to maintain our expected levels of profitability.

Although we have reallocated resources from the advanced manufacturing of solid-state lithium-ion batteries in order to focus on conventional cells, we expect to return to the solid-state chemistry as capital becomes more available for these longer term projects.
We expect to continue to make the necessary sales and marketing investments to enable the execution of our strategy, which includes expanding into additional end markets.

We expect our sales to increase in the next 12 months as our customers expand the number of models they include our battery systems in for the new model year and our entrance into new markets, trucking and industrials, with new product offerings.
We expect our cost of goods sold to increase over the next 12 months in conjunction with the anticipated increase in revenue.
We expect research and development expenses to remain relatively stable over the next year.
Looking forward, we anticipate that general and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue will decrease over the next 12 months.
We expect our selling and marketing expenses to decrease over the next 12 months due to cost reduction measures implemented in the second quarter of 2026.

Management evaluated the positive and negative evidence bearing upon the realizability of its deferred tax assets and determined that it is more likely than not that we will not recognize the benefits of the deferred tax assets primarily due to us entering into a 3-year cumulative loss position.

We expect our sales to increase in the coming quarters as our customers expand the number of models they include our battery systems in for the new model year and our entrance into new markets, trucking and industrials, with new product offerings.
We expect our Cost of goods sold to increase in conjunction with the anticipated increase in revenue over the next 12 months.

For example, a decrease in expected demand or sales prices, or an increase in the aging of inventory, could require us to increase our reserves, which would negatively affect our gross margin.
We recognize right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for our operating leases based on the present value of lease payments over the expected lease term.
We also make judgments regarding the lease term, including renewal and termination options, when it is reasonably certain that such options will be exercised.

We have historically been able to raise additional capital through issuance of equity and/or debt financing and we intend to raise additional capital as needed.
However, we cannot guarantee that we will be able to raise additional equity, contain expenses, or increase revenue, and comply with the financial covenants under the Term Loan.

estimates.name: Inventory Valuation
estimates.t: We maintain reserves for excess and obsolete inventory and for inventory that is carried at amounts in excess of its estimated realizable value.

estimates.name: Leases
estimates.t: Because our leases generally do not provide an implicit rate, we estimate an incremental borrowing rate to determine the present value of lease payments.

estimates.name: Business Combination
estimates.t: The Company’s accounting for business combinations requires significant judgments and estimates in determining the acquisition-date fair values of the consideration transferred, the assets acquired, including identifiable intangible assets, and the resulting goodwill.

statements.t: “Third quarter heavy-duty trucking revenue more than doubled sequentially to $1.3 million, in line with our August outlook, driven by expanding commercial fleet adoption,” commented Dr.
Based on our current order book, we expect trucking revenue to nearly double again in the fourth quarter on a sequential basis.
We expect new inventory to begin arriving toward the end of the fourth quarter, with broader availability and a more meaningful revenue contribution beginning in the first quarter of 2027.
We also expect Dakota to be accretive to Adjusted EBITDA as we leverage our existing infrastructure with minimal incremental overhead.”
Net sales were $12.2 million, below the Company’s previously issued guidance of approximately $13.5 million, and included $7.1 million in OEM net sales and $4.8 million in DTC net sales.
“Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we expect trucking revenue to nearly double sequentially as existing fleet customers expand their deployments and we onboard new fleets.

While RV market conditions remain challenging, we expect continued progress in trucking and Dakota Lithium, combined with our ongoing cost-reduction initiatives, to support our path toward profitability.

We also anticipate broader product availability and a more meaningful revenue contribution from Dakota Lithium beginning in the first quarter of 2027, with the acquisition expected to be accretive to Adjusted EBITDA as we leverage our existing infrastructure.
The Adjusted EBITDA outlook reflects the anticipated benefit of certain tariff-related refunds, along with continued progress on the Company’s cost-reduction initiatives.

* The Company cannot reconcile its expected Adjusted EBITDA under “Q4 2026 Guidance” without unreasonable effort because certain items that impact net (loss) income and other reconciling metrics are out of the Company’s control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted at this time.

risks.t: the timing and extent of recovery in the Company’s core markets, including the RV market
the Company’s ability to successfully increase market penetration into target markets
the Company’s ability to penetrate the heavy-duty trucking and other new markets
fluctuations in diesel fuel prices and their effect on fleet demand for the Company’s products
the growth of the addressable markets that the Company intends to target
the Company’s ability to successfully integrate Dakota Lithium and realize the anticipated benefits of the acquisition
the timing and amount of any tariff-related refunds and changes in tariffs or trade policy
the Company’s ability to retain members of its senior management team and other key personnel
the Company’s ability to maintain relationships with key suppliers, including suppliers in China
the Company’s ability to maintain relationships with key customers
the Company’s ability to protect its patents and other intellectual property
the Company’s ability to timely achieve the anticipated benefits of its licensing arrangement with Stryten Energy LLC
the Company’s ability to achieve the anticipated benefits of its customer arrangements with Stevens Transport
the Company’s ability to maintain the listing of its common stock and public warrants on the Nasdaq Capital Market
the Company’s ability to generate revenue from future product sales and its ability to achieve and maintain profitability
